subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Should OpenClaw solve the DeepSeek tool-result prefix-cache problem by hiding selected tool results from provider prompts, and exactly which tool names may be content-blind placeholders?
rationale: The patch changes model-visible semantics for first-class tools, and code review alone cannot decide whether hiding normal read/exec/web/memory observations is acceptable product behavior.

options.title: Narrow the policy first
options.body: Limit placeholders to maintainer-approved low-information heartbeat/session-status outputs or another explicitly proven set, then require live DeepSeek proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve normal tool outputs
options.body: Use heartbeat isolation, pruning, or another cache strategy that keeps read/exec/web/memory observations visible to the model by default.

options.title: Accept broad placeholders
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly accept the behavior change, but it should come with upgrade notes and proof that common agent workflows still work.

recommendation.title: Narrow the policy first
recommendation.body: Limit placeholders to maintainer-approved low-information heartbeat/session-status outputs or another explicitly proven set, then require live DeepSeek proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history signal is on the provider conversion and prompt-cache-adjacent runtime paths touched by this decision.
